stemBlocks.value: In quadrilateral PQRS, PQ is parallel to SR. The diagonal SQ = 8 cm, angle SPQ = 90 degrees, angle SQR = 82 degrees and angle QSR = 30 degrees. Determine (i) the length PS, (ii) the length PQ, and (iii) the area of PQRS.
Think first: The diagonal SQ splits the quadrilateral into a right-angled triangle and a non-right-angled triangle, and the parallel sides hand you the missing angle in the right-angled one.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p267-q01 from workbook page 267.

solutionSteps.instruction: Use the parallel lines to find angle PQS.

contentBlocks.value: PQ is parallel to SR and SQ is a transversal, so angle PQS = angle QSR (alternate angles) = 30 degrees.

solutionSteps.instruction: In right-angled triangle PQS, use SQ as the hypotenuse to find PS.

contentBlocks.value: PS is opposite the 30 degree angle: PS = SQ x sin 30 = 8 x 0.5

solutionSteps.instruction: Find PQ in the same triangle.

contentBlocks.value: PQ is adjacent to the 30 degree angle: PQ = SQ x cos 30 = 8 x 0.8660

solutionSteps.instruction: Work out the third angle of triangle QSR and use the sine rule to find SR.

contentBlocks.value: angle SRQ = 180 - 82 - 30 = 68 degrees, so SR / sin 82 = 8 / sin 68, giving SR = 8 x sin 82 / sin 68

solutionSteps.instruction: Find the area of each triangle and add them.

contentBlocks.value: Area PQS = (1/2)(4)(6.928) = 13.86 cm squared;  Area QSR = (1/2)(8)(8.544) sin 30 = 17.09 cm squared

strategyBlocks.value: Use the parallel sides to transfer the 30 degrees into triangle PQS, solve that right-angled triangle for PS and PQ, then find SR by the sine rule in triangle QSR and add the two triangle areas.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (i) PS = 4 cm  (ii) PQ = 6.93 cm (3 s.f.)  (iii) Area of PQRS = 30.9 cm squared (3 s.f.)

whyThisWorks.value: A diagonal turns any quadrilateral into two triangles, so its area is always the sum of the two triangle areas. The parallel sides let you move a known angle from one triangle into the other by the alternate-angle property, which is what makes the right-angled triangle solvable from a single length. Once two angles and a side of the second triangle are known, the sine rule fixes the remaining sides, and the formula (1/2)ab sin C gives the area without needing a perpendicular height.

commonErrors.misconception: Using the 82 degree angle as the angle in triangle PQS instead of the alternate 30 degrees.
